questions.stem: Find the nth term of the sequence: 7, 11, 15, 19, ...
questions.explanation: Common difference = 4. So starts with 4n. When n = 1: 4(1) = 4, but first term is 7. Add 3. nth term = 4n + 3. Check: n = 2 gives 11.

questions.stem: The nth term of a sequence is 5n - 2. Is 88 a term in this sequence?

options.text: No, because n is not a whole number

questions.explanation: Set 5n - 2 = 88. 5n = 90. n = 18. Since 18 is a positive whole number, 88 is the 18th term.
Common difference = -4. Start with -4n. When n = 1: -4, but first term is 25. Need to add 29. nth term = 29 - 4n. Check: n = 1 gives 25, n = 2 gives 21.

questions.stem: An arithmetic sequence has 3rd term = 14 and 7th term = 30. Find the nth term.
questions.explanation: Difference between 3rd and 7th = 30 - 14 = 16 over 4 gaps. Common difference = 4. 3rd term = 14, so 2nd = 10, 1st = 6. nth term = 4n + c where 4(1) + c = 6, so c = 2. nth term = 4n + 2. Check: n = 3 gives 14, n = 7 gives 30.

questions.stem: Which term of the sequence 3n + 7 first exceeds 100?
questions.explanation: Set 3n + 7 > 100. 3n > 93. n > 31. The first integer greater than 31 is 32. Check: 3(31) + 7 = 100 (not exceeding), 3(32) + 7 = 103 > 100.
